content:
After previewing it at the I/O 2026 conference in May, Gemini for macOS is now rolling out advanced voice control capabilities.

Google is positioning the feature as letting you "speak naturally across any window on your desktop," and it brings two main capabilities.

The first is smart voice input that can "transcribe what you say into clean, beautiful text." Gemini will automatically strip filler words like "um" and "uh," while also accounting for mid-sentence corrections to accurately capture what you meant to say.

The formatted text will be entered wherever your cursor currently is. This will provide a voice-to-text experience similar to Gboard Rambler on Gemini Intelligence phones, which is also rolling out.

The other capability goes beyond simple transcription and can understand what's currently on your screen, allowing it to perform complex tasks. This opt-in feature requires you to enable Gemini reasoning in your app's settings.

  • Capture and organize information: Highlight local files, images, or documents on your desktop and simply tell Gemini what you need. For example, you could say, "Look through these vet documents and email the boarding facility a summary of my dog's medical history."
  • Write and rewrite text: Highlight text anywhere on your screen and use your voice to instantly rewrite or adjust the tone, then drop the edited version directly where you need it. Try saying something like, "Rewrite these notes into an executive summary with a TL;DR at the top."
  • Generate and edit images: When you're brainstorming ideas or refining a travel itinerary, you can use voice to generate visual material; you can also reference designs on your desktop and ask for quick changes by voice. Try saying something like, "Take this illustration and generate a dark-mode version for me."

You can launch it by holding the Fn key anywhere in macOS, or by clicking the new screen-sharing button at the end of the "Ask Gemini" prompt box. Gemini will display a floating capsule button with a sound wave pattern at the bottom of your screen.

Make sure you've updated Gemini for macOS to the latest version (1.88). This new voice capability is rolling out globally to all users now, currently supporting English, with more languages "coming soon."
